Thanks for the thread, Lauren. Quick recommendations before we involve legal: 

1) Invoicing entity: We can bill Novus Holdings Ltd (UK) as long as accounting has an entity mapping in our billing system and the VAT certificate is verified. Operationally we prefer billing the US contracting party (Novus Health Inc) to keep the MSA and invoices aligned, but billing a different paying entity is common — we just need the PO and tax docs. Add a short clause in the Order Form: "Invoices may be directed to the paying entity identified on the Order Form; Redwood will rely on the paying entity details provided by Customer for tax and invoicing treatment."

2) VAT / withholding: If they will pay VAT on their side, ask legal to include a representation: Customer is VAT-registered and will provide certificate within X days; Customer bears VAT and any withholding taxes for amounts paid to Customer's local tax authorities (we'll add reciprocal language).

3) Net terms: Net 60 is long. Offer Net 45 standard, and accept Net 60 in exchange for either a small one-time activation fee paid at signing or a 2% on-invoice early-pay discount. If finance won't budge, we can accept Net 60 for enterprise but require PO in advance for the first invoice.

4) FX: If we invoice in USD but they pay GBP, include how FX will be applied: Redwood will invoice USD; Customer's bank may convert. For GBP invoicing we need to agree on the FX date (exchange rate as of invoice date or the payment date). Prefer to invoice USD and provide an optional converted-GBP line for AP convenience.

5) Operational asks: Request that the PO includes the paying entity legal name, billing address, VAT number (if outside US), and the AP contact.

I'll draft suggested redline bullets for order form language and pass to legal after you confirm.
